title: The US Army Has No Confirmed Leader — Civilian or Uniformed — Seven Months Into a War
subtitle: Dan Driscoll's resignation was covered globally as a Hegseth story. The military readiness dimension got one outlet.
body_md:
Dan Driscoll resigned as US Army Secretary on August 31 after 18 months in post. The White House offered no official reason. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had already fired Army Chief of Staff Gen. Randy George earlier in 2026. The result, as [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/09/01/army-secretary-dan-driscoll-resigns-hegseth) reported, is that "the military's largest service" is now "without Senate-confirmed leadership, civilian or uniformed" — seven months into the Iran war.

Only one outlet led with that operational fact. [The Hindu Intl](https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/us-army-secretary-driscoll-submits-resignation-white-house/article71413517.ece) reported the resignation "could effectively leave the Army without permanent civilian or uniformed leadership" with the Iran war entering its seventh month. Every other outlet framed it as a Hegseth story.

The Hegseth framing was accurate. [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/08/31/hegseth-dan-driscoll-trump-administration) identified the two proximate causes: "the feeling that his modernization initiatives were being blocked, and the chaos created by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's firing of senior generals." [The Atlantic](https://www.theatlantic.com/ideas/2026/08/hegseth-driscoll/688480/?utm_source=feed) called it "the latest sign of severe dysfunction in the Defense Department" and titled it "Hegseth's Pentagon Lurches off the Rails." [The Independent](https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/pete-hegseth-pentagon-firings-dan-driscoll-b3042619.html) reported Trump was "surprised" by the scale of the Pentagon purge — attributing presidential unease with Hegseth's pace of dismissals.

The cross-ideological spread of the dysfunction framing is notable. [CBC World](https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/army-secretary-dan-driscoll-resigns-trump-administration-9.7327311?cmp=rss) described it as "the latest departure of a top military leader during the second Trump administration." [Hindustan Times](https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/us-news/us-army-secretary-dan-driscoll-resigns-after-reported-tensions-with-pete-hegseth-101788251224339.html) and [Daily Wire](https://www.dailywire.com/news/trumps-army-secretary-makes-surprise-move-after-reported-hegseth-clash) — a right-leaning US outlet — both confirmed the Driscoll-Hegseth rupture. Daily Wire contextualized it in wartime: "American forces came under Iranian missile fire over the weekend after the US struck Iranian launchers near the Strait of Hormuz," using the combat context to amplify rather than minimize the leadership gap. [Breitbart](https://www.breitbart.com/politics/2026/09/01/u-s-army-secretary-dan-driscoll-steps-down-after-18-months-in-the-post/) was the exception: the only outlet to quote the White House's "Secretary of War" label for Hegseth and present the resignation as orderly MAGA-agenda success with no acknowledgment of dysfunction.

US outlets alone surfaced the political triangle underneath. [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/08/31/hegseth-dan-driscoll-trump-administration) identified that Driscoll's friendship with Vice President Vance — they were Yale Law classmates — had itself become a source of tension with Hegseth. [Daily Wire](https://www.dailywire.com/news/trumps-army-secretary-makes-surprise-move-after-reported-hegseth-clash) noted that Driscoll "was also trusted with an assignment that had little to do with his official Army job when Trump sent him into the Russia-Ukraine diplomatic fight last year." Both facts — the Vance friendship and the Russia-Ukraine diplomatic role — disappeared in international coverage, which reported the story as standard leadership turnover.

Germany and Australia are absent from the corpus. Germany's absence means the EU's leading NATO contributor's perspective on US Army leadership stability is unrepresented. Australia's absence is more pointed: AUKUS links US and Australian defense postures directly, and the Army's leadership vacuum has specific implications for joint operational planning.

[France 24 Spanish](https://www.france24.com/es/ee-uu-y-canad%C3%A1/20260901-ee-uu-dan-driscoll-renuncia-como-secretario-del-ej%C3%A9rcito-tras-meses-de-tensiones-con-hegseth) noted — uniquely — that as of its reporting, Trump had not yet formally accepted the resignation. That procedural question, unresolved when most outlets treated the departure as settled, points to the asymmetry between the speed of political reporting and the pace of institutional change: a war is in its seventh month, and whether the Army's civilian leadership is formally gone or merely announced as such was, at the time of publication, still technically open.
